owner: akiendelllinux_cc_0 (CC) gates writes. inference_domain owns the seam being filled (Law 6).
intention: Wire inference_domain's `resolver` seam to the real local inference host, so the compile-once path actually reaches a model — and so `yield_report()` produces REAL numbers instead of measuring a stub.
why: MEASURED 2026-07-26. inference_domain sits on the build order as DONE and the librarian is planned on top of it. Its own filed edge (b) says: 'THE HOST CLIENT is injected (the `resolver` seam) and not yet wired to a real host — it will live HERE and nowhere else.' The record was honest at the component and wrong at the plan. Worse: a working host has been running on this box the entire time and nothing in Cairn knew — `ollama serve` (pid 2136) up since 2026-07-22, listening on :11434, with qwen2.5:7b, llama3.2:1b and nomic-embed-text. Both endpoints measured working on 2026-07-26 (embeddings returned 768 dimensions; generation responded). Nothing in the tree references port 11434, ollama, or that endpoint. THE SECOND WHY IS THE BIGGER ONE: `yield_report()` measures tokens SPENT on misses against tokens AVOIDED by hits. That is the instrument for telos aim 1 — the measured curve of resolver-calls declining as the corpus grows. Akien's most showcaseable claim (a prebuild step saving ~90% of tokens, independently reimplemented at his workplace and running daily) has no recorded measurement inside Cairn. This node is what turns that instrument on.
traces_to: telos aim 1 — demonstrate inference compilation. Unmeasurable until the meter reads a real host.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. The cache's yield is currently a hypothesis measured against a stub.
Law 6 — the host client lives in inference_domain and nowhere else; this node fills that seam and adds no second path.
Law 8 — the sole-path tooth (a tester import-scan that reds any other module opening the host) is inference_domain's own filed edge (b), and this node is what makes that tooth worth growing.

gates.prove_gate: proof gate — the tester runs the proof and emits a VALIDATION.

falsifier: Against the REAL host: (1) a first request resolves and returns an answer; (2) an IDENTICAL second request is a HIT and the resolver is NEVER called — asserted by instrumenting the resolver, not inferred from timing; (3) `yield_report()` shows tokens AVOIDED strictly greater than zero, and the avoided/spent numbers reconcile against the two calls. That is the compile-once claim proved end to end rather than asserted. A hollow build fails (2) — returning a cached-looking answer while still calling the host is exactly the failure this must catch. Additionally the host's ABSENCE must be a declared, loud failure, not a crash: the box can be rebooted, the service can be down, and 'inference host unreachable' is a legitimate measured state (Law 7).
horizon: The yield number is meaningless until real traffic runs through it. Re-read once the librarian or the reading work has driven a few hundred requests — before then the curve has too few points to say anything, and quoting it early would be the same error as quoting an unmeasured 90%.
distinctions_recorded: THE HOST IS NOT HEX. `hex` does not resolve, is not in /etc/hosts, and is not on the ARP table — the M1 remains a plan. What exists is ollama on THIS box. That is fine and it is the point of the seam: build and prove against localhost now, and Hex later becomes a HOST SWAP behind the same seam. The librarian therefore does NOT wait on acquiring or wiring an M1, which is a materially different dependency picture from the one held-librarian assumed.

EMBEDDINGS ARE A DIFFERENT CALL SHAPE AND ARE NOT IN SCOPE HERE. inference_domain does completion-shaped caching; nomic-embed-text is an embedding endpoint. Both live on the same host, but wiring the completion resolver does not give the system embeddings, and pretending otherwise would repeat the done-but-not-connected defect this node exists to close. Whether Cairn wants a pretrained embedder AT ALL is Akien's open call — his objection stands ('every call is an inference call', so the curve never bends), with the word graph as the real answer and an off-the-shelf embedder at most a bootstrap that must carry a written exit condition.

THE OLDER EMBEDDINGS ENDPOINT CANNOT BE METERED. /api/embeddings returns ONLY the vector — no prompt_eval_count, no eval_count. Measured 2026-07-26, and it changed the build: resolving through it would have produced a working resolver whose every cost was 0, and yield_report — the instrument for the whole Telos 1 claim — would have reported a flawlessly consistent 0-spent/0-avoided. The shape right, the content hollow, and nothing red (Law 8). host.py uses /api/embed and RAISES HostUnmetered rather than defaulting a missing counter to 0: an unmetered answer is not cheaper than no answer, it is a lie about the thesis.

A FALSIFIER MADE MACHINE-CHECKABLE. Charter edge (c) carries a falsifier for T1.4 without evaluating it. A time horizon on a temperature-0 completion is theatre — nothing rots as the clock moves — so horizon is '' and the falsifier is 'model_digest(<model>) == <sha>', answerable by one /api/tags read. The edge stays open, but closing it is now a comparison rather than a design problem. Sampling is pinned to temperature 0 for the same reason: caching a nondeterministic call silently changes what the cache MEANS.

THE FIRST LIVE ROW CAUGHT WHAT 16 GREEN TEETH DID NOT. The run was green and the row it wrote said 'model_digest(nomic-embed-text) == <unread at resolve time>': the host tags the model 'nomic-embed-text:latest', the caller names it 'nomic-embed-text', and the dict lookup missed. So the falsifier degraded silently for the MOST COMMON way to name a model. Visible only by reading the record the run actually wrote (Law 3 — the proof attested the shape, only the live row showed the content was empty). Fixed, and the fixture now carries the ':latest' the host really reports, because a tidied fixture would have kept the proof green through the bug.

SOLE-PATH IS NOW RE-CHECKED, AND THE CHECK TESTS CAPABILITY NOT MENTION. Charter edge (b) said 'sole by construction' — a claim about the present that nothing re-ran. A tooth now scans the tree on every proof run. Written as a grep for ':11434' it flagged base/needs.py, where the string sits in a docstring, an error-message example and a test fixture: prose ABOUT a measurement, unable to open a socket. A check that cannot tell a door from a description of one gets trained away by its own noise — and would still miss a module that reads the endpoint from config. So it asks which modules can DIAL: outbound imports by full dotted name. Exactly one does. web_server/daemon.py imports http.server, which LISTENS and cannot reach anything — that distinction is the tooth's, not an exemption.

SEMANTIC CANONICALIZATION (edge a) is untouched: canonicalize is structural (sorted-key JSON) and does not collapse paraphrases. Real traffic through a real host is what will show how much that costs, which is the evidence that edge has been waiting for.

(RULED BY AKIEN 2026-07-27 — CLOSED, THEN CC'S WRITE-UP CORRECTED BY HIM THE SAME DAY.) His words: 'all requests go by graph trees, word or fact, and escalate on graph failure to a node depositing call that validates by resubmitting the same request.' The host is NEVER in the answer path: on a graph miss it supplies NODES, they are deposited, and the ORIGINAL REQUEST IS RESUBMITTED — the graph resolving it is the validation. CC's option (a) was wrong. TWO CORRECTIONS TO CC'S FIRST WRITE-UP OF THIS EDGE, both recorded in notes/held-librarian.json: the phrase 'the graph type is a coordinate, not a class' was CC's inference recorded as Akien's ruling (fabricated attribution, the exact failure that note already documents); and CC dropped the resubmit-validates clause, which is the half that closes the loop. THE LIVE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS COMPONENT (CC's read, unmeasured): the resubmit path can LIVELOCK against this node's cache — same request canonicalizes to the same key, hits, and returns the nodes that just failed to resolve, while yield_report() counts each turn as tokens AVOIDED. A backfill call is not cacheable on the request alone; the key or falsifier must carry the graph state it failed against. Filed against this node, not built, and it supersedes CC's earlier 'a cache hit on backfill is a defect signal' — it is a trap the meter reports as a saving.

(FILED) yield_report() raises psycopg2 UndefinedTable when the cache table has never been created, rather than reporting an empty meter. Found this run — the real inference_calls table had never existed outside a proof's ephemeral run. Loud is right (Law 7), but the diagnosis points at SQL instead of at 'no traffic yet'. Left alone rather than changed unasked; it is a diagnostic-surface polish, not a defect in the meter.
